subject: Re: MAP: unit-econ deep dive and eval gating for HelixMed POC
messages:
From: James Lawson <james.lawson@helixmed.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: MAP request: economics check before POC kickoff

Neha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we lock dates for the POC and share with engineering, procurement needs a short MAP item that validates the unit economics assumptions. Two specific asks from our side:

1) A concise tokens-per-dollar calculation for a 6-week POC (expected 250k requests, average 350 tokens in request+response).
2) Assumptions and mitigations for caching and batching we should plan for to avoid cost blowouts and keep p50 latency < 400ms.

Can your team produce a brief itemized check (spreadsheet ok) that we can attach to the MAP? We need this for our financing review next Thursday.

James
James Lawson
Head of Integrations, HelixMed
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: James Lawson <james.lawson@helixmed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP request: economics check before POC kickoff

James —

Thanks, we can do that. Quick note on scope: we'll produce a 1-page unit-econ summary + a simple spreadsheet that models tokens/$ across a few scenarios (baseline, cached prefixes, optimistic batching).

High-level assumptions we'll use (happy to tweak):
- Model variant: rdx-2.7b-quant (inference price baseline: $0.000275 per output token on hosted plan)
- Average tokens per roundtrip: 350 (you provided)
- Expected POC volume: 250k requests over 6 weeks (≈35k req/week)
- KV/prefix cache hit rate scenarios: 0%, 30%, 60%
- Batching: no batching (1x), conservative (batch size 4), aggressive (batch size 12) — impacts throughput and per-token amortized overhead

We will deliver by EOD Wednesday our MAP-ready spreadsheet and a short summary for procurement. I'll loop in Ben for any projection detail.

- Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, James Lawson <james.lawson@helixmed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: RE: MAP request: economics check before POC kickoff

Attaching the draft spreadsheet (helixmed_map_v3.xlsx) and a short notes CSV (tokenization_profile.csv). Key items pulled into the sheet:

- Per-token cost assumptions: output token cost $0.000275, input token cost assumed $0.00009 (internal accounting).
- Roundtrip tokens: median 120 input / 230 output = 350 total.
- Base unit cost (no cache, no batching): 350 * ($0.00009 + $0.000275) ≈ $0.1237 per request. For 250k requests => $30,925.
- With 30% KV/prefix cache hit (i.e., 30% of requests served from cached prefix so only 40 tokens served): effective avg tokens/request ≈ 0.3*40 + 0.7*350 = 0.3*40 + 0.7*350 = 12 + 245 = 257 tokens => ~ $9.5k reduction (~$21.4k total).
- Batching effect: with batch size n, we amortize fixed attention overhead and reduce per-request CPU overhead; conservatively we see a 12% cost reduction at batch=4, 28% at batch=12 (applies mainly to high-concurrency server-side workloads). Note: batching increases p95 latency tail if not carefully tuned.

Risk notes:
- If traffic is extremely spiky and we rely on low cold-cache warmup, token costs can be 15–25% higher in first 48h of major ramps.
- Quantization profile may change per-customer model; we used rdx-2.7b-quant baseline.

Next steps (MAP items):
1) Redwood to provide the spreadsheet + one-pager (Wed EOD) — Owner: Ben
2) HelixMed to confirm target cache hit (goal) and acceptable p95 latency — Owner: James — Due: Thu 2 Dec
3) Agree on gating: if projected 6-week cost > $40k, schedule a short call to review routing/quantization alternatives — Owner: Neha — Due: Fri 3 Dec

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: helixmed_map_v3.xlsx (xlsx), tokenization_profile.csv (csv)
From: James Lawson <james.lawson@helixmed.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP request: economics check before POC kickoff

Ben / Neha —

Received, thank you. A couple clarifications from procurement:
- Our finance team uses tokens/$ with the following split: they want to see both hosted list pricing and an internal effective price assuming 15% enterprise discount. Please include both columns.
- For caching, our product team expects ~45% prefix reuse for the triage flows (we'll validate with sample logs). Please show an intermediate row at 45% hit.
- p95 latency target is 700ms for now; p50 must be < 400ms. Will the batching scenarios preserve that?

We can confirm the sample logs by EOD Fri. If numbers land below $25k for the POC after a 15% discount, procurement will fast-track.

-James
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: James Lawson <james.lawson@helixmed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP request: economics check before POC kickoff

James —

Following up with the finalized MAP item we discussed. Summary highlights (also in attached spreadsheet):
- Two columns provided: hosted list price and effective with 15% enterprise discount.
- Key scenarios (total POC cost for 250k req):
  * Baseline (0% cache, no batching): list $30,925 — discounted $26,286
  * Mid (45% cache, batch=4 conservative): list $18,020 — discounted $15,317
  * Optimistic (60% cache, batch=12): list $12,850 — discounted $10,922

Latency impact: batch=4 preserves p50 < 400ms in our perf runs; p95 increases by ~120ms if not paired with autoscale headroom. Batch=12 shows p50 ~340ms but p95 pushes toward 820ms unless you provision extra concurrency and use routing to dedicated pool. We recommend batch=4 for the POC.

MAP action items (finalized):
- Redwood: provide final spreadsheet and short one-pager (done) — Ben — completed 2026-12-09
- HelixMed: confirm sample logs and target cache hit (45% stated) — James — due 2026-12-10
- Joint: schedule a 30-min operations runbook call to validate autoscale windows and batching parameters before kickoff — Owner: Neha — propose 2026-12-15

If procurement signs off at the middle row (45% cache, batch=4) we'll proceed to schedule engineering onboarding. If you prefer, I can convert the spreadsheet rows into MAP checklist items for signature.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if you want to go line-by-line.

-neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
